verdict.reasoning: Patient says she has been feeling really anxious "over the past few months" and "get really nervous every morning about leaving the house".

She reports feeling like this for "maybe about two months or so" and that it "coincides with me starting a new job" which is "quite stressful"; she works "for a fashion retailer in the head office team" and says "My boss is not very nice to me."
She describes waking with "my heart kind of racing, and then I'm just, like, panicking that I'm going to be late" and also waking "in a panic thinking I'm going to be late."
She says the palpitations feel "Irregular, I think" and that they last "a couple of minutes" and on another occasion "lying there...for, like, 10 minutes."
When asked about chest pain she replies: "No. Well, yeah, it's painful when the heart. When my heart is being fat, but yeah," indicating discomfort during palpitations.

She reports she "can't get to sleep for hours and hours and hours," that she is "lying awake all night," and estimates "maybe three, four hours I'm getting now," adding that even when asleep "it's such a shallow sleep."
In daytime she reports "It's just really, really low" energy and being "so tired that anything that previously was really fun is just not enjoyable."
She says she finds "no enjoyment at all kind of day to day in anything that I'm doing" and that activities that were previously fun are "just not enjoyable," which is consistent with anhedonia.
She notes she is "on edge the whole time," which reflects feeling on edge/irritable; explicit word "irritability" is not used but the clinical description matches.
She says she avoids friends: "I avoid them in so much that I feel like I'm... I know that I'm not going to have fun because I don't want to go out and do things that I would normally have done."
She previously exercised: "I did used to like to go running and to play tennis and stuff," but now "it's just not. I'm just not enjoying it. I'm not like, I'm not going out to do that quite so much."
She continues to attend work: "I think I've always managed to make it to work" but says "I do pretty much every morning I think, oh, I should call it sick."

She describes ongoing anxiety linked to work with worsening: "I've been feeling like this...about two months" and later "I have felt it get worse and worse over the past," suggesting daily/worsening anxiety over weeks.
She reports persistent low mood: "I'm pretty much down. Like, I don't enjoy being with my day at all" and "constant feeling of just being a bit down, a bit unhappy."
When asked about severity she states: "I haven't had any suicidal thoughts or any thoughts that have been that extreme."
She notes family support: "I have a good support system. Like, I do have a good family and stuff."
The doctor suggests self-referral to NHS talking therapy and one-to-one therapy; she answers "Yeah, yeah, I think so" and later "That's great, I look forward to reading it," indicating receptiveness.
